Jev ranks better. It never got the chance.

Measured on production on 2026-09-21: with the 150 ms per-keystroke budget, 0 of 72 real calls were ranked by Jev. Every one aborted and fell back, while still adding about 152 ms to each keystroke. Given room to finish, Jev puts the right page first more often than the deterministic order: 12/12 against 10/12 on known answers.

Raising the budget alone is the wrong fix, because a 1000 ms block per keystroke is worse than today. This PR takes the call off the keystroke path instead: the deterministic list paints at once, the request goes out on a typing pause, and the answer is applied only if the query has not moved on.

Type and watch the two designs diverge

Try mcp, then keep typing without pausing. Nothing here touches the network: Jev latency is sampled from the measured distribution (min 708.7, p50 760.5, p95 825.6, max 863.9 ms).

idle
ranked by deterministic 0 calls · 0 ranked · 0 discarded · ~$0.0000

The before mode aborts at 150 ms, so the counter never leaves 0 ranked while the cost keeps climbing: that is the production behaviour, and the old route reported $0 for every one of those calls. The after mode waits 450 ms of idle, allows 1000 ms, and discards any answer whose query you have already typed past.

Why 1000 ms, and not 300 or 750

Measured from Israel with prod's exact payload and no abort, so it includes a round trip the Vercel route does not pay. 1000 ms is the first budget that returns an answer at all, and it is affordable only because nothing on screen waits for it.
